key_insight: Augmenting 2D image-based localization with per-image estimated depth maps captures local geometry so you can get strong geometric reasoning and accurate poses without building a centralized 3D reconstruction.
problem_solved: Closes the gap between easy-to-build, easy-to-update 2D image-based localization (which lacks effective geometric reasoning) and accurate but cumbersome 3D structure-based methods (which require centralized reconstruction and are hard to update).
method: Represent each reference image by the image plus an estimated depth map to encode local 3D structure.
Perform dense image matching between query images and depth-augmented reference images to establish geometric correspondences for pose estimation.
Keep a decentralized, image-based database that is simple to build and update while leveraging depth for improved geometric accuracy.
impact: Enables practical, scalable localization that combines the maintainability of image-only systems with stronger geometric reasoning—useful for robotics, AR, mapping, and large-scale deployment where frequent updates are needed.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison: plain 2D image localization vs. depth-augmented image localization (show differences in matching/accuracy).
Pipeline diagram: depth estimation → dense matching → correspondence filtering → pose estimation.
Overlay of dense correspondences between query and reference images with depth-informed reprojections to show geometric consistency.
Iconic illustration contrasting centralized 3D reconstruction (single heavy model) with decentralized image+depth database (many lightweight, updatable entries).
paper_title: ImLoc: Revisiting Visual Localization with Image-based Representation
paper_authors: Xudong Jiang, Fangjinhua Wang, Silvano Galliani, Christoph Vogel, Marc Pollefeys
